content.value_statement: Database query code can be slow, fragile, or vulnerable to injection. This skill guides secure SQL and ORM patterns for reliable data access.
actual_capabilities: Recommends parameterized queries for SQL and ORM code.
Guides eager loading to reduce N+1 query problems.
Suggests indexes, selected columns, and pagination for performance.
Supports transaction planning for related database operations.
Covers filtering, sorting, joins, and repository query logic.
limitations: Does not inspect live database query plans automatically.
Does not replace a database security review.
Requires project schema and data access patterns for precise advice.
Depends on an external relative standards file until remediated.

use_cases.title: Build a Repository Query
use_cases.description: Create data access methods with clear filters, sorting, and pagination.

use_cases.title: Improve Query Performance
use_cases.description: Find opportunities for eager loading, indexes, and smaller result sets.

use_cases.title: Review Data Access Safety
use_cases.description: Check query logic for injection risks, missing transactions, and unsafe raw SQL.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Query
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one database operation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this database query for safety, performance, and readability. Suggest changes that match the backend-queries guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Design Data Fetching
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan data access for a new endpoint.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the data fetching logic for this endpoint. Include filters, pagination, selected fields, and safe parameter handling.

prompt_templates.title: Fix N Plus One Queries
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this data loading flow for N+1 queries. Recommend eager loading or batching changes with expected tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Transaction
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a transaction for these related database writes. Include rollback behavior, locking concerns, and query timeout guidance.

output_examples.input: Review a user list endpoint that loads profiles and roles separately.
output_examples.output: The response identifies a likely N+1 pattern, recommends eager loading related records, and suggests paginated results with selected fields.

output_examples.input: Plan a query for searchable orders with status filters and date ranges.
output_examples.output: The response recommends parameter binding, stable sorting, pagination limits, and indexes for status and creation date.

output_examples.input: Review a payment update that writes several related records.
output_examples.output: The response recommends one transaction, clear rollback behavior, timeout limits, and careful handling of concurrent updates.

best_practices: Provide schema details and expected result sizes before asking for query guidance.
Ask for both security and performance review when using raw SQL.
Validate recommendations against your database engine and ORM behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not concatenate user input into raw database queries.
Do not load all columns or all rows when a narrow result is enough.
Do not split related writes across multiple operations without a transaction plan.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps write safer and faster backend queries for SQL, ORM, and repository code.

faq.question: Can it prevent SQL injection?
faq.answer: It guides parameterized query patterns, but reviewers must verify the final implementation.

faq.question: Does it support ORM code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance covers ORM methods, query builders, eager loading, and repository patterns.

faq.question: Can it tune production databases?
faq.answer: No. It can suggest query improvements, but production tuning needs real metrics and query plans.

faq.question: Is it useful for transactions?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help plan related writes, rollback behavior, and consistency boundaries.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
